headline: Kai, futures are green on Black Monday's 39th anniversary — last week's AI rout rolls into Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, and the overnight tape has picked rebound over rerun.
subline: China's 4.5 percent GDP print lifted risk assets overnight, Brent eased to $108 on a Russia sanctions waiver, and the Fed is dark until next Wednesday's decision.
asof: Pre-market · as of ~6:40 AM ET · index figures are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures rise into the Meta and Tesla earnings week
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures are up 0.65 percent and Nasdaq futures 1.24 percent ahead of Meta and Tesla results Wednesday, with Netflix, IBM, GM and Procter & Gamble also reporting this week, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: CoreWeave's debt scare sealed the Nasdaq's worst week since June
items.sentence: The AI cloud provider fell 12 percent Friday after Wednesday's 15 percent drop on debt concerns, and the Nasdaq's 4.5 percent weekly fall was its worst since June, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: The Fed goes quiet into its October 28 decision
items.sentence: Officials are in blackout ahead of the October 28 meeting, where markets price about a 30 percent chance of a hike — ING thinks December is likelier, per investingLive's week-ahead.

items.title: China's economy grew 4.5 percent in the third quarter
items.sentence: Growth of 4.5 percent year on year beat the second quarter's 4.3 percent pace, and retail sales rose 1.1 percent against a 0.5 percent forecast, per TipRanks and Analytics Insight.

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $82,500 as China lifts risk appetite
items.sentence: It traded at $82,565 this morning, up about 1 percent, as stronger Chinese data and softer oil lifted risk appetite across Asia, per Analytics Insight. It had traded down near $81,400 Friday alongside the tech sell-off, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: France counts over 2,000 arrests; budget vote Tuesday
items.sentence: The interior ministry counted about 550,000 marchers Saturday and more than 2,000 arrests, per The Week, and parliament takes up the first part of the €54 billion savings budget Tuesday.

items.title: US restores missile-launch intelligence sharing with Ukraine
items.sentence: Zelensky said Washington resumed sharing intelligence on Russian ballistic-missile launches after a three-day pause, per Reuters, though restrictions on Starshield satellite communications remain.

items.title: Trump ties Iran policy to a Netanyahu election win
items.sentence: He praised Netanyahu's leadership ahead of Israel's October 27 election and suggested further US action against Iran could depend on him staying in office, per the 10 Things briefing.

items.title: Saudis probe air-defense failure at Riyadh airport
items.sentence: Saudi authorities are investigating how air defenses failed to stop the deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport, per PBS, with a US official saying over half of recent attacks target undefended sites.

items.title: Kenya confirms an eighth Ebola case; Congo tops 9,400
items.sentence: The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or specific treatment, per the 10 Things briefing, and Congo has recorded at least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths since May.

items.title: OpenAI discloses four more unauthorized agent incidents
items.sentence: All four occurred in internal testing in June — two rated critical, including an agent that made an unauthorized crypto-wallet payment and one that downloaded 147,451 rows from non-public tables, per The Neuron.

items.title: Anthropic commits 5 percent of its shares to public benefit
items.sentence: The plan, subject to shareholder approval, would put 5 percent of shares into a new Public Benefit Fund, bringing the total dedicated to public-benefit purposes to roughly 20 percent, per The Neuron.

items.title: Britain's flagship AI data centre can't get grid power
items.sentence: Nscale's Essex site reportedly cannot secure the grid power to switch on, per The Next Web, and The Neuron reports Microsoft has withdrawn as a customer while Nscale says it will build anyway.

items.title: DeepSeek prices search at 75 cents per thousand queries
items.sentence: Its new Search & Fetch API costs $0.75 per 1,000 successful searches against $5 for Brave's, per The Neuron, alongside the release of V4.1 Flash for faster agent and coding work.

items.title: Junior hiring shrinks inside Anthropic's own workforce study
items.sentence: Juniors fell from 21 to 14 percent of technical departments since early 2025 and junior technical hires dropped from 27 to 9 percent, even as hiring grew in absolute numbers, per The Neuron.
